label: UNKNOWN-DEPLOYMENT
claim: The deployed cache filesystem and mount stack were not supplied; no filesystem-specific durability claim is made.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Persistent mode targets a local Linux filesystem and block stack only. NFS, SMB/CIFS, FUSE, overlayfs, virtiofs and clustered filesystems require separate contracts.

label: A-GUARANTEE
claim: Same-filesystem rename can atomically replace a target name in the namespace.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Namespace atomicity does not by itself establish crash-durable publication.

label: A-GUARANTEE
claim: A successful file fsync/fdatasync does not necessarily persist the containing directory entry; synchronize the directory explicitly.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Use fdatasync for immutable payloads whose required metadata is limited to retrievability and size; use fsync when other inode metadata is part of the format contract.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Create the unpublished inode in the target directory/filesystem; cross-mount rename is rejected and cross-directory durability broadens the sync set.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Prefer O_TMPFILE only after a runtime capability probe; retain a named O_CREAT|O_EXCL fallback.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: An object write is successful only when the accumulated result exactly equals the requested object length.

label: A-GUARANTEE
claim: A positive write result may be short and must be followed by writes of the remaining range.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: A completed write or write CQE is not a persistence boundary.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: A direct-I/O error can leave part of the requested region written and inconsistent; reject the object rather than infer all-or-none behavior.

label: A-GUARANTEE
claim: Buffered writeback errors and ENOSPC can surface at file synchronization rather than at the original write.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: fallocate is an optional space-management step, not a replacement for exact writes, validation, or synchronization.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: ENOSPC or EDQUOT at create, allocation, write, file sync, namespace mutation, or directory sync fails the transaction and forbids acknowledgement.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Treat EIO as a root-level health event: stop acknowledgements, fence the writer, retain diagnostics, and require recovery/operator action.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Do not retry close after an error; perform the decisive fsync/fdatasync first and record close errors diagnostically.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Published cache objects are immutable; updates create a new inode and replace a name or manifest pointer.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Publication order is: create unpublished inode, exact write, validate, file sync, atomic publish, directory sync, then acknowledge.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Synchronize every directory whose entry set changed; prefer one parent directory to keep the durability boundary explicit.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Avoid cross-directory publication. If unavoidable, synchronize both source and destination directories and test the precise operation.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Overwrite policy permits atomic whole-inode replacement, not in-place mutation of a published object.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: RENAME_EXCHANGE is atomic name exchange only; it does not eliminate file-sync or directory-sync requirements.

label: A-GUARANTEE
claim: ext4 data=ordered orders associated data before the transaction metadata commit; delayed allocation remains enabled by default.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: ext4 auto_da_alloc is a compatibility heuristic for broken applications and is not the selected application durability primitive.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Do not support ext4 data=writeback for persistent mode without a separately proven contract.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: ext4 data=journal disables delayed allocation and O_DIRECT; do not assume the normal DIO profile under that mount mode.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Keep ext4 ordering barriers enabled and reject nobarrier unless the complete nonvolatile cache claim is independently proven and tested.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: XFS buffered writes use delayed allocation; explicit file and directory synchronization remains the baseline.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: XFS wsync may be evaluated as an optimization/HA option but is not part of the portable application contract.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Btrfs COW, snapshots, compression and reflink alter allocation and sharing behavior; immutable publication avoids mutable shared-extent assumptions.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Btrfs nodatacow implies nodatasum and permits interrupted in-place updates to be partial; do not combine it with mutable published objects.

label: TEST-REQUIRED
claim: Btrfs support is conditional on near-full data and metadata, snapshot, reflink, compression, and recovery tests on the deployed profile.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Discard/TRIM reclaims storage and can affect latency; it is neither a durability boundary nor a secure-erasure guarantee.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Direct-I/O alignment must be queried with statx when available; never hard-code 4096 as a portable alignment.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Do not mix buffered I/O, O_DIRECT, and writable mmap for one object; do not fork with in-flight DIO using private mappings.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: An io_uring CQE proves only the submitted operation result; durability follows only from successful sync CQEs and the tested storage stack.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: For writes, require CQE res to equal the submitted length; res > 0 but short is not a chain-breaking error.

label: A-GUARANTEE
claim: Registered files and pending requests hold kernel file references; closing the userspace descriptor does not cancel them.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Registered-buffer updates/replacements can leave old resources alive after the update returns; tagged release CQEs identify terminal release. Explicit UNREGISTER_BUFFERS is documented synchronous, while ring-shutdown unpinning can complete asynchronously.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Cancellation is racy. Handle target and cancel CQEs in either order and accept completion, independent failure, -ECANCELED/-EINTR, -ENOENT, and -EALREADY as documented.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Linked operations sequence execution but do not validate application-level success. Check every CQE and do not blindly link a potentially short write to fsync.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Graceful teardown: stop submissions, cancel/drain outstanding requests, unregister resources, observe release tags, then queue_exit.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Encode operation kind, object generation, and slot generation in user_data; do not reuse state until all terminal CQEs are consumed.

label: A-GUARANTEE
claim: Linux 7.1.3 implements IORING_OP_FSYNC via vfs_fsync_range and maps IORING_FSYNC_DATASYNC to the datasync argument.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: The final crash boundary depends on filesystem, block layer, device, firmware, RAID/dm/hypervisor and power-loss behavior honoring flush/FUA.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Use exactly one writer process per cache root; give HaloKV and the RPC tensor cache separate roots and lock files.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: flock/OFD locks are advisory and released with the open-file-description lifetime; all participating writers must cooperate.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Classic process-associated fcntl locks can be dropped by closing any descriptor for the same file and are not the preferred writer fence.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: A local advisory lock is not durable fencing, lease arbitration, or a multi-host consensus mechanism.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: OPEN-FMT-01 should use an immutable self-describing object with magic, version, declared length, checksum/hash, object identity, and generation.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: HaloKV and model-tensor cache share the primitive but retain separate format namespaces, roots, admission/eviction policy, and writer fences.

label: A-CONSTRAINT
claim: Do not report success to a caller until directory synchronization succeeds after publication.

label: RECOMMENDATION
claim: Startup recovery validates object header, exact length and hash before making an object live; orphan temps and corrupt generations are quarantined or removed.

label: TEST-REQUIRED
claim: Record and enforce filesystem type, kernel, mount options, block topology, DIO alignment and O_TMPFILE support as a certified profile.

label: TEST-REQUIRED
claim: Documentation selects candidate primitives; only the implementation and local kill/ENOSPC/EIO/power-cut matrix can establish the deployed contract.
